title: How fine is a decimal of latitude?
hook: A latitude can run to many decimals. What does the last digit measure?

knows: that coordinates can be written with many decimals
that latitude is measured in degrees
doesNotKnow: what each decimal place means on the ground
that each extra decimal is ten times finer

misconception: Four decimal places of latitude resolve a point to the centimetre.
objective: The learner can say that the fourth decimal of latitude is about 11 m, the fifth about 1 m and the sixth about 0.1 m, and that extra digits are finer than a phone can measure.

claims.text: A degree of latitude is about 111 km on a sphere.
claims.source: 6,371.0088 km x pi / 180 = 111.195 km (kit EARTH_RADIUS_KM). On the WGS84 ellipsoid a degree of latitude is about 110.6 km at the equator to about 111.7 km at the poles (from memory; needs a checker).

claims.text: One step of the fourth decimal of latitude is about 11.1 m, the fifth about 1.11 m, the sixth about 0.111 m.
claims.source: 111,195 m x 10^-4, 10^-5, 10^-6. Stage bar and readout use the same function, stepMetres(). Builder's node check: 11.12, 1.112, 0.1112 m; 111.2 m at 3 decimals; 11.1 km at 1.

claims.text: 11 m is about a tenth of a football pitch's length.
claims.source: 11.12 / 105 = 10.6%. Pitch length 105 m is a common international size (FIFA/IFAB recommend 105 x 68 m; from memory, the laws allow a range; needs a checker).

claims.text: Phone GPS is typically good to a few metres in the open, so digits past the fifth mostly record noise, not position.
claims.source: From memory, not re-checked: GPS.gov states smartphone GPS is typically accurate to about 4.9 m (16 ft) under open sky. 'Mostly noise past the fifth digit' is the builder's inference (1 m versus several metres). Needs a checker and a link.

claims.text: The stage is a toy: a schematic bar drawn to scale beside a 105 x 68 m pitch on a sphere; it moves north only.
claims.source: Model label on the stage. Longitude steps are shorter at this latitude and are not shown.

recall.question: Each extra decimal place of a latitude makes the position how much finer?
recall.why: A decimal place is a factor of ten: about 11 m at four places, 1 m at five, 0.1 m at six.
